prior_importants.description: moduleOf's new rule (no extension in the last segment means a directory) treats a test-helper path ending in a sentence period, or a wildcard under test/<kind>/, as a module. That gives a false module-boundary trigger and a design the ticket doesn't need.

For chore and refactor, `Scope boundary` is marked `area: true`. Both the form and the rubric ask that field to name what the change leaves alone, so paths the ticket stays out of fire the module-boundary and ADR-area triggers.

When the area names a file by its GitHub permalink, the extracted path starts with `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/`. That path matches no ADR glob and no module, so `adr-area` and `module-boundary` don't fire and the design gate passes when it should fail.

findings.description: `HEADING` runs on every line outside a fence. Its lazy capture is followed by `\s*#*\s*$`, so a single line like `# a` + N spaces + `b` costs about N³/6 backtracking steps and blocks the event loop of whatever process runs intake.
findings.body:
**ReDoS: `HEADING` backtracks cubically on one crafted line of the issue body**

```ts
const HEADING = /^#{1,6}\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$/;
```

`sections()` runs this on every line of the untrusted issue body that is outside a fence.

**Trigger:** one line, `"# a" + " ".repeat(N) + "b"`. Tabs or NBSP work in place of the spaces.

**Why it is cubic:**
- The lazy `(.+?)` grows one character at a time.
- At each length, two greedy `\s*` loops sit back to back across the remaining j spaces. `#*` can only match empty on a space, so it adds nothing.
- Every split between the two loops is tried, about j²/2 of them, and each fails at `$` on `b`.
- In total that is about N³/6 steps. V8's irregexp has no memoization.

N = 5,000 is about 2e10 steps, tens of seconds. At GitHub's 65,536-character body limit it is about 4.7e13 steps, hours of a pinned core. The issue author controls the body, including edits made after `ready` is applied, and decision 176's intake will pass that body to `checkTicketIntake`.

**Fix:** the end trim is redundant. `normalize()` already turns `#` and whitespace into spaces and trims them. A greedy capture with no end anchor runs in linear time and gives the same keys:
- `## Goal ##` still gives `goal`.
- `## C#` still gives `c`.
- `#Goal` and a lone `#` still are not headings.
- Every case in the current tests passes.

The one change is that a whitespace-only `##   ` line no longer closes the section before it.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c6972069753379843cf91959184b44101e5e2ef4/src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts#L81-L82>
findings.suggestion:
/** A Markdown heading of any level; `normalize` drops a closing `#` run with the other punctuation. */
const HEADING = /^#{1,6}\s+(\S.*)/;

findings.description: PLACEHOLDER only matches the bare token, so in a terse field a placeholder with a trailing period or Markdown wrapping passes as filled: Affected area `TBD.`, Suspected area `Unknown.`, Source PR `N/A.` or Time box `` `n/a` `` are reported complete, while the same text without the period is flagged vague.

EMPTY_LIST_ITEM is tested with the `m` flag across the whole field, code fences included, so any pasted unified diff that adds or removes a blank line (a line that is just `+` or `-`) marks a fully filled Reproduction, Expected against actual, Findings, Scenarios or Proof field as vague.
findings.body:
**A `+` or `-` line inside a fenced diff counts as an empty list item**

```ts
const EMPTY_LIST_ITEM = /^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])(?:\s+\[[ xX]?\])?\s*$/m;
...
if (text === '' || PLACEHOLDER.test(text) || EMPTY_LIST_ITEM.test(text)) return true;
```

`sections()` tracks fences only to keep headings from being read inside them. Fenced lines still go into the field's value. `isVague` then runs the multiline `EMPTY_LIST_ITEM` over the whole value, fences included. In `git diff` output, an added blank line is exactly `+` and a removed one is exactly `-`, and both match `^\s*[-*+]\s*$`.

**Trigger:** a bug whose `Expected against actual` holds a fenced diff:

````
Actual: the generated hook gains an extra block:
```diff
 exit 0
+
+echo stale
```
````

This returns `vague: ['Expected against actual']`, so intake removes `ready` from a complete ticket. The same happens to a follow-up's `Findings` or `Scenarios` that quote a patch, and to a chore's proof that pastes such output. Fenced values are expected input: the tests already cover fenced Reproduction and Suspected area.

An empty bullet outside a fence still flagging the field is the tested intent and is not in question here. A diff line inside a fence is not a list item.

**Fix:** skip fenced lines when testing `EMPTY_LIST_ITEM`. For example, have `sections()` also record each field's non-fenced lines and test those.

findings.description: A path-like glob such as `src/**/*.ts` or `src/**` in `Files in scope` (the form asks for "One path or glob per line") becomes the single module `**` and matches no ADR glob, so a repo-wide refactor fires neither trigger.
findings.body:
**A glob in an area field fires neither `module-boundary` nor `adr-area`**

The chore/refactor form's `Files in scope` asks for "One path or glob per line" (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/chore-refactor.yml:40`). Trace a refactor with `Files in scope: src/**/*.ts` and `adrAreas: ['src/claude/**']`:

1. `PATH` (line 95) extracts `src/**`. `*` is not in `[\w.-]`, so the repeated group stops at `src/`, and the final `[\w.*-]+` takes `**`. Nothing else in the string matches.
2. `moduleOf('src/**')` sees no extension on `**`, counts it as a directory, and returns `'**'`. `modules` is `{'**'}`, size 1, so `module-boundary` does not fire.
3. `globToRegExp('src/claude/**')` gives `^src/claude/.*$`. It fails against both `src/**` and `src/**/`, so `adr-area` does not fire.

```ts
const directories = /\.\w+$/.test(parts.at(-1) ?? '') ? parts.length - 1 : parts.length;
if (parts[0] === 'src' && directories > 1) return parts[1];
...
adrAreas.some((area) => area.test(path) || area.test(`${path}/`));
```

The result is `triggers: []` and `needsDesign: false` for a change scoped to every module and every ADR area. Decision 176 forces a design on any ticket that touches an ADR area or crosses a module boundary. No test uses a glob as input.

This is the opposite failure from the still-open `test/helpers/*` thread. That one is a false module; this one is a glob that covers several modules collapsing into one.

**Fix:** treat a wildcard in the module segment as crossing modules. For ADR areas, count a hit when one side's literal prefix, up to its first wildcard, is a prefix of the other's.

findings.description: Follow-up has no `area` field, so its whole body feeds the triggers. The scope globs and paths used as inputs in `Scenarios` then fire adr-area or module-boundary falsely. `Findings`, which the form defines as "the file and line it points at", is the real area field.
findings.body:
**Follow-up reads its whole body for triggers, so input paths in `Scenarios` fire them**

```ts
const areaText =
  areaFields.length === 0
    ? body
    : areaFields.map((field) => sectionMap.get(normalize(field.heading)) ?? '').join('\n');
```

Follow-up is now the only type with no `area` field. The fix commit gave docs and spike their own area fields. The follow-up form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/follow-up.yml:24`) and the rubric (`docs/tickets/follow-up.md:13-14`) say `Findings` holds "the file and line it points at". `Scenarios` holds "the input or sequence that shows it", and the rubric's own example input is a scope (`../x`).

**Trigger:** a follow-up with:
- `Findings: - [minor] src/core/plan.service.ts:88 the error names the path`
- `Scenarios: pup plan add t-1 --scope src/claude/** prints the path, not the task id`
- `adrAreas: ['src/claude/**']`

`src/claude/**` from Scenarios matches the ADR glob, and the modules are `{core, claude}`. `adr-area` and `module-boundary` both fire, so a finding that touches only `src/core` is forced through design.

**Fix:** mark `Findings` as the area field. The "reads the whole body" test stays green because its paths sit in `Findings`, though its name would need updating. The `areaFields.length === 0 ? body` branch would then have no user.

findings.description: `PATH` takes a trailing period into the last segment, so `Suspected area: The parser in src/core/glob.utils.ts.` produces `src/core/glob.utils.ts.`. That fails to match an ADR file glob like `src/core/*.utils.ts` (both `path` and `path/` are tried), and adr-area does not fire. This is a sibling of owed finding (1), so fix it in `PATH`, not only in `moduleOf`, or the ADR path keeps the bug.

Both regexes use the `m` flag with a leading `^\s*`, and `\s` matches `\n`. So every line start in a run of N blank lines scans to the run's end and backtracks: about N²/2 steps per regex. A 65k-newline field or body costs about 2e9 steps each (several seconds). This is separate from the already-raised "DEPENDENCY_BOX on whole body" scope point. Fix: use `[ \t]` in place of `\s` in both, e.g. `/^[ \t]*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])(?:[ \t]+\[[ xX]?\])?[ \t]*$/m` and `/^[ \t]*[-*+][ \t]+\[[xX]\].*\bdependenc/im`.

The first alternative of the global `PATH` regex has nothing anchoring where it can start. On `"a".repeat(N)` with no `/`, every start index runs `[\w.-]+` to the end and backtracks looking for `/`: about N²/2 steps. That is about 2e9 at N=65k, in an area field, or anywhere in a follow-up body since that type is read whole. Fix: add a lookbehind, `(?<![\w.-])(?:[\w.-]+\/)+[\w.*-]+|...`. Matches stay the same, because a later start in the same run always reaches the same `/`.

SIZE_CAP_LINES = 600 is declared in a behavioural utils file and duplicates DIFF_SIZE_FLAG_LINES (600) in src/core/constants/merge-gate.constants.ts:5. general.md says "Thresholds, timeouts, tool names, path fragments — none are inlined at the use site. They go in the area's `*.constants.ts` as a named export". The sibling merge-gate.service.ts imports its 600 from a constants file. The two copies can drift if decision 173's cap changes. Import DIFF_SIZE_FLAG_LINES, or move the constant into a core/constants file.

`What changes, or the question` is marked `area: true`, so code paths named in a spike's question count as touched. Example: `Can src/claude/hooks.ts race src/core/gate.service.ts?` with Form of the answer `docs/spikes/x.md` fires adr-area or module-boundary, though the spike only writes the doc. For docs, `Form of the answer` already names the pages changed.

The purity test rebuilds the repo root with join(import.meta.dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'src', ...) even though the ROOT constant is defined at line 9. Use join(ROOT, 'src', 'core', 'ticket-intake.utils.ts'). This goes away if the purity block above is deleted.

The six 'names a missing <type> field' tests (lines 32-85) share one shape: a body missing one field, with the missing heading asserted. Fold them into one it.each over [type, fields, expectedMissing] rows. That removes about five repeated it() and checkTicketIntake call blocks. The feature case also asserts vague is empty, so keep that in the table or leave it out.
